title: Follow up, stay honest, and track your numbers

say: Follow up, stay honest, and track your numbers.
This is the video for Module 3 of Client Acquisition Basics.
Silence after your first message rarely means no. Business owners are busy, and messages get buried.

panel.rule: Every follow-up adds value. Never just 'checking in'.

say: For example, Ngozi, the bookkeeper, messages a pharmacy owner on 3 March. No reply.

panel.heading: Ngozi turns 'not now' into a client
items: Day 0: offer to tidy monthly records

say: Her day 4 reminder gets an answer: 'Not now, very busy with stock taking.'

panel.heading: Ngozi turns 'not now' into a client
items: Day 0: offer to tidy monthly records

say: She replies calmly: 'Understood. Shall I check back after your stock taking, perhaps early April?' The owner says yes, and Ngozi notes the date in her sheet.

panel.heading: Ngozi turns 'not now' into a client
items: Day 0: offer to tidy monthly records

say: On 2 April she sends a one-page checklist of records a pharmacy should keep, and asks for a 10-minute call.

panel.heading: Ngozi turns 'not now' into a client
items: Day 0: offer to tidy monthly records

say: On the call she qualifies with BANT and proposes a 3-month clean-up at about 60,000 naira a month, an illustrative price. The owner pays a 50% deposit. Without the follow-up, that 'not now' would have been forgotten.

say: Small, specific, true claims persuade better than 'best' or 'guaranteed'. Say 'I have done bookkeeping for two clinics and a supermarket', not 'many big companies'. Ask permission before using a client's name, words or logo.

Never write reviews yourself, invent urgency, or promise results you do not control. And when someone says 'please stop', stop at once. Mark them 'do not contact' and remove their number, in the spirit of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.
Track five numbers every Friday: contacted, replied, calls, proposals, won. Each rate is one stage divided by the stage just before it.
For example, Halima contacted 40 schools and 14 replied. That is 35%.
She held 5 calls from those 14 replies, about 36%.
She sent 4 proposals and won 2. Her proposals and messages are working well.
So her weak stage is turning replies into calls. Her one change: offer two specific times instead of 'let me know when you are free'. Change one thing, and test it for 2 to 4 weeks.
Also track your time. Halima spends about 6 hours a week, so 24 hours a month, on outreach.
Each new school pays about 45,000 naira for the trial, then about 80,000 naira for the following month.
Two clients means two of each.
That is about 250,000 naira of work from 24 hours of outreach, roughly 10,400 naira per outreach hour. Outreach is valuable work, not wasted time.
So remember. Follow up four times, adding value each time. If someone says it is too expensive, offer a smaller scope rather than cutting your rate. Stay honest, and stop the moment someone asks.
Small numbers jump around, so collect a month of data before you judge.

panel.heading: Key points from Module 3
items: Silence means busy: plan four spaced touches
'Too expensive': reduce scope, not your rate
True claims, permission, stop when asked
Track five numbers, change one thing
